## Milestone gates
- **M0** (S01–S03): every app logs in against the hub; CI green.
- **M1** (S04–S08): a shortage finds eligible sources, and one accepts with a hold, in the hospital app. Passed 2026-10-07 on the merged S05–S08 tree: `make e2e` 4/4 (Scenario 1 across two browser contexts: A reports, B declines, A's match re-runs without B) with `make worker` running and `PLAYWRIGHT_CHROMIUM_PATH=/opt/pw-browsers/chromium`.
- **M2** (S09–S13): the full loop from shortage to reconciliation across all three apps, with audit and copilot.
- **M3** (S14–S19): chat, forecasts, surplus, optimization, cold chain, Critical mode.
- **M4** (S20): three demo scenarios pass three times in a row.

- [S01 → S03] TypeScript is pinned to `~6.0.3`: typescript-eslint 8.71 only supports TS `<6.1.0`, and TS 7 is `latest` on npm. Keep apps on 6.0.x until typescript-eslint supports TS 7.
- [S01 → S03] Root `pnpm typecheck` / `pnpm test` run `pnpm -r --if-present`, so they are no-ops until apps/packages add `typecheck` and `test` scripts. Replace the `client-drift` CI placeholder with the real regenerate-and-diff check.
- [S02 → S03] `make client` is still the S03 placeholder, so no client was generated in S02. `GET /orgs/{id}` returns `OrgOut | PublicOrgView` and `GET /orgs/{id}/facilities` returns `Page[FacilityOut] | Page[PublicFacilityView]` (own org vs other org); the generated types are unions.
- [S02 → S03] Starlette's `TestClient` now warns that it wants `httpx2`; hub tests use `httpx.AsyncClient` + `ASGITransport` instead. Don't introduce `TestClient`.

- [S11 delivery-web → S16/S20] "Share location" runs only while `/driver` is open (it stops when the driver leaves the page or the phone suspends the tab); pings omit `ts`, so the hub stamps its own time (a phone clock more than 5 min ahead would otherwise get 400s). A background tracker would need a native wrapper or a service worker.
- [S11 delivery-web → S16] `/plan` (Route planner) is still the placeholder. (Resolved in S16.)
- [S16 → S11] A parallel S11 fix adds a 409 at assign for a shipment whose holds span several facilities of the source, "until S16 lifts it". S16 did not lift it: the planner still gives each shipment one pickup (the facility with the largest held share, `shipments.service.stops_of`), and `/routes/apply` goes through `assign`, so such a shipment makes the whole apply 409 (all or nothing). Lifting it needs one PICKUP leg per facility and a pickup node per facility in `optimizer.plan`; a separate change.
- [S16 → S20] The route starts at its first pickup now: drivers have no depot or position on record (the last `LocationPing` of a current job could seed it). Live re-planning and several drivers at once are out of scope. `POST /routes/apply` re-plans, so the result can differ from the plan the dispatcher saw if travel times or deadlines moved; the screen shows what the hub assigned.
- [S16 → S20] The real OSRM `/table` call was not exercised here (no Docker); tests use a fake provider or haversine. With 25 shipments the table is 50 × 50 in one request.
- [S16 → tooling] Root `pnpm test` runs every package's Vitest at once; on this 4-core box under a load average of ~25 (other agents) some UI tests in hospital-web, supplier-web and delivery-web hit their timeouts. Each package passes alone and `pnpm -r --workspace-concurrency=1 test` passes (70 + 104 + 59 + 25 + 21).
- [S11 delivery-web → S20] The delivery-web bundle is 614 kB minified (Leaflet included); Vite warns over 500 kB. Code-split the map if load time matters on phones.
- [S11 delivery-web → S11/specs] (Changed by the S11 review fixes, 2026-10-08: the hub now refuses a box on a CREATED shipment, 409, and on a shipment another org carries, 403; see the new delivery-web follow-up.) Display choices, no rule changed: the assign dialog lists only active drivers (the hub answers 400 for an inactive one); the fleet's device picker offers only this org's shipments on the way (ASSIGNED, PICKED_UP, IN_TRANSIT) without a box, although the hub would also accept a CREATED one; the detail page offers attaching a box until the shipment has arrived, and taking it off at any time (after delivery that frees the box for the next trip).

- [S12 hospital-web → S12 hub] (Resolved in hospital-web part 2: `useLatestRecommendation` reads `GET /shortages/{id}/recommendations/latest`; `unavailable` is gone.) **S12 HUB HOOK**: `useCurrentRecommendationId(shortageId, runId)` in `apps/hospital-web/src/api.ts` is the only place the app finds a shortage's recommendation. Until the hub's "current recommendation for a shortage" read lands it reads one page (200 rows) of `GET /audit?entity=recommendation` and takes the `recommendation.created` row whose `after.match_run_id` is the latest match run's id. That needs `audit.read` (APPROVER, ADMIN): a requester without it sees only "A recommendation is awaiting a decision" while the shortage is AWAITING_DECISION. Swap the body for the new endpoint, keep the return shape `{id, isPending, error, unavailable}`, key it by its path template, and drop `unavailable`; then the decision panel works for every user of the org.
- [S12 hospital-web → S12 part 2] (Resolved in part 2, except the dashboard's "deliveries due today", a Dashboard row owned by S08/S18 that is still not built.) Receive screen (`/deliveries/:id/receive`, `receipt.record`, needs `POST /shipments/{id}/receipt`; link it from DELIVERED rows of `/deliveries`), notifications UI (escalations; needs a notification read endpoint), the dashboard's "deliveries due today", and the residual shortage link (`parent_shortage_id`) on shortage detail.
- [S12 hospital-web → hub] (Resolved in part 2: the tab reads `GET /shortages/{id}/audit`.) The audit tab finds a shortage's purchase orders and shipments from their `.created` rows (`after.shortage_id`, first 200 of each type) and only the current recommendation (older, rejected or expired ones have no link from the shortage). A `GET /audit?shortage_id=` (every row of the shortage and its records) would replace the lookups.
- [S12 hospital-web → hub] A mirrored audit row (business-rules §10) is recognised in the app (`isMirrored` in `apps/hospital-web/src/display.ts`) as `actor_id` null with a user's reason (USER, or "No reason was entered."); a system change always has a factual cause. The acting org is named from what the org already sees (the request's source, the PO's `supplier_org_id`, the shipment's from or carrier org), else "Another organization". An `actor_org_id` (or `mirrored_from_org_id`) on `AuditOut` would let the hub say it directly.
- [S12 hospital-web → hub] (Resolved in part 2: `GET /shipments?direction=inbound`.) `/deliveries` keeps the shipments whose `to_org_id` is the caller's org from `GET /shipments` (which also returns outgoing transfers), page by page. A `?direction=incoming` filter would avoid near-empty pages; outgoing transfers are not shown anywhere in hospital-web yet.
- [S12 hospital-web → tests] `fakeHub` returns the same `Response` object on every call to a route, and a body can be read once: give a route that several queries call (e.g. `GET /audit`) a handler, `() => hubError(...)`.
- [S12 hub → S12 hospital-web] Endpoints (api-and-events.md S12 rows; regenerated client): decision panel `GET /shortages/{id}/recommendations/latest` (404 until one exists) with the S09 approve/reject/escalate; Deliveries `GET /shipments?direction=inbound` (status, `eta`/`planned_eta`, `requires_cold_chain`); Receive `GET /shipments/{id}` (`qty` is expected; `inspection_note_required`; `receipt` once recorded) and `POST /shipments/{id}/receipt {received, accepted, rejected, condition, inspection_note?, expiry_date?, batch_no?, reason?}` → 201 `ReceiptOut` (`reconciliation` null until every shipment of the shortage has one). The form needs an expiry date field whenever accepted > 0 (400 `details.reason = expiry_date_required`) and an optional batch number (409 `conflict` if used). Audit tab `GET /shortages/{id}/audit` (`audit.read`, oldest first; label by `reason_source`). Notifications `GET /notifications?unread=true`, `POST /notifications/{id}/read`. `EVENT_QUERIES` now also refreshes `/shortages/{shortage_id}/recommendations/latest`, `/shortages/{shortage_id}/audit` and `/notifications` (on `recommendation.status_changed`).
- [S12 → S15] `has_open_excursion(session, shipment)` in `app/shipments/service.py` returns False; replace it with the ColdChainEvent query (an EXCURSION with no later RECOVERED? §11 says the excursion "stays on record" after recovery; decide what "open" means). The receipt gate and the detail's `inspection_note_required` both call it; `test_an_open_excursion_needs_an_inspection_note` patches it.
- [S12 → S19] Reconciliation does not recompute reliability (§12 "after each reconciliation") or write CreditLedger rows; both belong to S19. Reconciliation rows carry per-shipment `discrepancy` for the discrepancy rate.
- [S12 → specs] (Partly resolved in the S11 review fixes, 2026-10-08, with the user's decisions: (2) the PO DELIVERED trigger is now in business-rules §8; (3) the residual now inherits the parent's `excluded_org_ids`, §9, so a source that declined, had a recommendation rejected or rejected a PO is not asked again.) Open questions, implemented literally (no business rule changed): (1) §9 gives the new batch no expiry, batch number or cost, so the receipt takes `expiry_date` (required when accepted > 0) and an optional `batch_no`; unit cost is the PO price for a purchase and 0 for a transfer (the source's cost must not reach the receiver; a 0 cost ranks that stock cheapest if it is ever offered); the batch is unverified (`last_verified_at` null), so it fails freshness until verified and no stock-change re-run is triggered at receipt; (2) the PO moves DISPATCHED → DELIVERED when the buyer records the receipt (§8 names no trigger), as a SYSTEM row in the hospital's org mirrored into the supplier's; (3) the residual keeps the parent's facility, `required_by`, `source` and `created_by` (§9 names only product, priority and shelf life), its notes are empty, and it does not inherit the parent's excluded (declining) sources, so B may be asked again; (4) Reconciliation `outcome` is the shortage's (CONFIRMED or PARTIAL, the same on every shipment's row) with a per-shipment `discrepancy`; accepted above the shortfall counts as RESOLVED; (5) the inspection note is required whenever an excursion is open, even when nothing is accepted (the brief's wording; §9 says "before accepting"); (6) the move to RECEIVED carries the receiver and their reason (as approval does for IN_FULFILLMENT); RESOLVED/PARTIALLY_RESOLVED, the reconciliation and the residual are SYSTEM rows stating recorded figures; (7) `reconciliation.completed` goes to the shortage's org only; sources see RECONCILED through `shipment.status_changed` and never see the receipt (CLAUDE.md rule 6).
- [S11 fixes → S11 delivery-web] The shipment detail offers "attach a cold box" until the shipment has arrived, and the fleet picker lists ASSIGNED, PICKED_UP and IN_TRANSIT shipments of this org. The hub now answers 409 for a CREATED shipment (no carrier yet) and 403 for one another org carries; hide the attach action while CREATED. After an unassign or re-assign the box is off the shipment (`device_id` null), so the page should show it as detached.
- [S11 fixes → S16] `POST /routes` reusing `shipments.service.assign` will hit the multi-facility 409 for exactly the shipments it exists to plan: move or bypass that check there, and update business-rules §8 (the limitation) in the same change.
- [S11 fixes → hub] `assign_device` locks the device then the shipment, while assign/unassign lock the shipment then update its device; a dispatcher attaching a box at the same moment another unassigns the same shipment can deadlock (Postgres aborts one; the client sees 500). Rare; a shared lock order would remove it.
- [S09 → hub, resolved 2026-10-08] Rejecting a recommendation now excludes its sources from the shortage's later runs (business-rules §7 step 6); the recommendation explanation names them "(was in a recommendation the requester rejected)", and a residual's explanation adds "for the earlier shortage" to an inherited exclusion.
- [S12 → S20] (Resolved in hospital-web part 2: `e2e/tests/scenario1-receipt.spec.ts` and the full suite passed.) `make e2e` was not run for S12 (hub on :8000 not allowed here; the screens are not built yet). Scenario 1 steps 4-7 are covered by the API test `test_scenario_1_short_delivery_opens_a_residual_of_60_that_is_matching`.
- [S12 hospital-web → S20] `pnpm test` runs every package's suite in parallel, and under load supplier-web's `orders.test.tsx` ("Scenario 1 step 6 …", "shows new purchase orders …") hit Vitest's 5 s test timeout once in four runs on 2026-10-08. hospital-web now has `src/test/setup.ts` (`asyncUtilTimeout` 4 s, `testTimeout` 20 s); give supplier-web (and delivery-web) the same shared setup in their next section.
- [S12 hospital-web → S15] The Receive screen labels the inspection note "required" and says "this shipment had a cold-chain excursion" whenever the hub sends `inspection_note_required`; once S15 defines an open excursion, show the excursion itself (cold-chain panel) next to the note.
- [S12 hospital-web → hub] The unread count on the bell is the length of the first page (200) of `GET /notifications?unread=true` ("200+" when there is a next cursor). An unread count in the response (or `GET /notifications/unread-count`) would make it exact.
